A spectator waves a US flag as Pope Leo XIV leaves his weekly general audience in St Peter's Square at the Vatican on October 28, 2026 [Gregorio Borgia/AP Photo]By Al Jazeera Staff, AP and ReutersPublished On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026
Pope Leo XIV has become the first pontiff to vote in a United States general election after casting a mail-in ballot in Chicago, where he was born.
The Vatican confirmed on Friday that the pope submitted a mail-in ballot in the city ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, citing his longstanding belief in civic participation.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3What polls say as Trump reverses course on cancelled campaign rallieslist 2 of 3Trump reverses course, reinstates cancelled campaign rallieslist 3 of 3US appeals court again rejects Trump bid to set aside California ballotsend of list
Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen”, as he has done “whenever he was eligible to do so”, the Vatican’s press office said.
“The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added.
The Vatican did not say which candidates Leo voted for.
In a note commenting on Leo’s vote, the US Conference of Catholic Bishops urged Catholics to put “our faith before our politics” and “uphold human dignity and the common good”.
“In voting, our Holy Father sets the example that encourages each citizen to exercise their civic responsibility,” said the conference’s director of public affairs, Chieko Noguchi.
Leo is a citizen not only of the US but also of Peru, where he lived as a priest and bishop for more than 20 years, as well as of the Vatican, where he is head of state.

Experts warn that fake pollsters could weaken trust in election data [File: Stephen Maturen/Getty Images via AFP]By Evan SemonesPublished On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026
Fabricated political polling has forced its way into the spotlight during the midterm election period in the United States.
Revelations that a small number of fraudulent firms have released fictitious results – some of which were picked up by news outlets and polling trackers – have raised concerns about how easily false information can acquire credibility.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3What polls say as Trump reverses course on cancelled campaign rallieslist 2 of 3Trump reverses course, reinstates cancelled campaign rallieslist 3 of 3Trump administration renews bid to block Alaska election resultsend of list
Those datasets can be used to cast doubt on the electoral process. And when bad actors are unmasked, their existence can be leveraged to undermine voter confidence in election information overall.
The latest example occurred earlier this month, when Wedgewood Polls released a statement on social media admitting its statistics about a bevy of battleground states – like Texas, Ohio, Michigan, Kansas and Maine – were fake.
Wedgewood described its work as “an experimental project” designed to highlight the “vulnerabilities, lack of oversight and overall low barrier to entry” in the US polling industry.
“Having previously worked in the polling and research sector, we watched as the public’s trust in polling eroded alongside a rise in unverified, low-quality methodology,” the firm said in a statement posted to its social media account, which has now been deleted.

Workers install wooden boards over the windows of a luxury boutique in Berlin, Germany, on October 30, 2026, ahead of a planned protest [Ebrahim Noroozi/AP]By Al Jazeera Staff and AFPPublished On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026
Germany and France are preparing for potential protests over the weekend that could coincide with Halloween festivities.
Approximately 150,000 people in Germany have registered to turn out in about 30 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Cologne, to protest on Saturday.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3What European students can learn from their Serbian peerslist 2 of 3France braces for ‘very high risk’ of disorder at Halloween protestslist 3 of 3Italy tightens security as students, unions launch nationwide protestsend of list
Police plan to deploy thousands of additional officers across the country. Some luxury jewellery shops and clothing stores have boarded up windows to protect against potential looting or violence.
Protests in Germany are led by a group dubbed “GenZ regelt!”, which translates to “Gen Z has got this!”.
The German protest movement’s complaints include the high cost of living, poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, politicians taking decisions with little regard for the younger generation.
A wave of largely youth-led protests has swept across Europe in recent weeks, many with similar complaints: rising prices, declining educational facilities and what many protesters see as a lack of prospects for their future.
France braces again
Many of those grievances mirror those of the youth-led protests that have convulsed French cities and towns for three consecutive weekends.
Shops and businesses in Paris and other cities were boarding up windows on Friday.

Brazil has summoned Argentina’s top diplomat in the country to answer questions about right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who fled first to Argentina, then to the United States, after losing Sunday’s presidential election.
On Thursday, Brazil’s Foreign Ministry called in Argentina’s charge d’affaires, Maria Emilia Cortes, sources inside the government told the news agency Reuters.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after losing Brazil’s presidential electionlist 2 of 3What’s next for Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro after election defeat?list 3 of 3Trump says won’t ‘take sides’ in Brazil election, but calls it a ‘disgrace’end of list
Argentina’s Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, however, has denied on social media that his government received a formal request for explanations regarding Bolsonaro’s decision to flee into Argentina late on Tuesday.
The circumstances surrounding Bolsonaro’s departure threaten to further strain relations between Brazil’s recently re-elected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his Argentinian counterpart, libertarian Javier Milei.
After Sunday’s election, Bolsonaro was given a deadline to surrender his passports. Officials ordered him to remain in the country as part of an ongoing legal case.
He is part of an ongoing investigation into a money-laundering scheme, known as the Banco Master scandal.

Suspended Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Swieczkowski speaks with a megaphone as protesters gather outside the headquarters of Poland's Constitutional Court building in Warsaw on October 30, 2026 [Wojtek RADWANSKI/AFP] (AFP)By Al Jazeera Staff, AP and ReutersPublished On 30 Oct 202630 Oct 2026
Polish police have been deployed outside the country’s top court after demonstrators gathered to protest the suspension of its head judge.
Police said on Friday they entered the premises of the Constitutional Tribunal after incidents outside the court, including objects being thrown at police.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Three injured in third school attack in Poland in less than a weeklist 2 of 3Polish police probe alleged plot to assassinate PM Tusk, defence ministerlist 3 of 3Thousands protest across Poland for access to free and legal abortionsend of list
Protesters descended on the Warsaw court after it announced on Friday that its head, Bogdan Swieczkowski, had been suspended.
His suspension is related to a long-running dispute that has effectively paralysed the court.
Over the past six months, Swieczkowski used his power as head of the court to block judges elected by the current parliamentary majority from assuming their court duties.
Minister of Justice Waldemar Zurek told reporters on Friday that he had requested that Swieczkowski and his deputy’s immunity be lifted for failing to fulfil their duties by preventing judges from performing their work.
Swieczkowski was appointed to his position by Poland’s former nationalist Law and Justice party (PiS) government, which critics have accused of politicising the country’s courts.

The world's largest tech companies depend on volunteer-built, open-source web infrastructure that is increasingly vulnerable to security flaws [File: Dado Ruvic/Illustration/Reuters]By Umar FarooqPublished On 30 Oct 202630 Oct 2026
Earlier this month, authorities worldwide urged website administrators to execute emergency updates after a nonprofit programming foundation flagged critical security flaws that could allow hackers to breach systems.
Government and corporate websites briefly went offline to patch the vulnerabilities, nicknamed PHP2Shell, which were discovered by independent cybersecurity experts using artificial intelligence (AI).
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3What’s the PHP coding flaw that could pull down 70 percent of the internet?list 2 of 3World leaders warn of security flaws found in PHP programming languagelist 3 of 3OpenAI says its agents turned off own safeguardsend of list
The vulnerabilities were embedded in the code of a widely used open-source web programming language, PHP, for more than a decade. They had gone unnoticed, however, because it would have been too complicated for humans to exploit them without the use of advanced AI.
But cybersecurity experts, as well as those maintaining important software, say PHP2Shell could be the first in a deluge of security flaws exposed by emerging AI. They say much of the world’s most critical digital infrastructure is maintained by volunteers, who often lack the resources and time to respond to newly discovered threats.

US President Donald Trump has targeted the East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, DC, for a renovation [File: Saul Loeb/AFP]By Al Jazeera Staff, Reuters and The Associated PressPublished On 30 Oct 202630 Oct 2026
A United States federal judge has opened a “formal inquiry” into whether US government lawyers misled the court over plans to transform a historic public golf course in Washington, DC.
Friday’s manoeuvre escalates an ongoing legal fight over President Donald Trump’s efforts to reshape the US capital.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Demonstrators in US form human chain to protest Kennedy Center closure votelist 2 of 3Trump says monumental arch in Washington, DC will also be military complexlist 3 of 3Trump’s planned DC arch faces new lawsuitend of list
Judge Ana Reyes of the US District Court for the District of Columbia announced she would appoint a special master to examine whether government officials withheld information or made misleading assertions concerning the East Potomac Golf Links.
The inquiry will not establish whether government lawyers committed misconduct. It will instead determine whether their conduct breached professional or ethical obligations.
The inquiry follows a series of contradictory statements by administration officials about plans to renovate the course, notably after Trump announced he would proceed with the project on social media.
Reyes questioned Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr for more than two hours during Friday’s hearing, repeatedly comparing his testimony with the president’s online announcements.
She also asked him whether a National Park Service official had been instructed to omit details from a court declaration.
